paragraphs.sourceText: Listen to the following passage. Altogether the passage will be read to you four times. During the first reading, which will be done at normal speed, listen and try to understand the meaning. For the second and third readings, the passage, except the first sentence, will be read sentence by sentence, or phrase by phrase, with intervals of 15 seconds. The last reading will be done at normal speed again and during this time you should check your work. You will then be given ONE minute to check your work once more.
paragraphs.translationZh: 听下面这段话。这篇文章总共会读给你四遍。在第一次阅读时，将以正常速度完成，聆听并尝试理解其含义。第二、三读时，除第一句外，逐句或逐词朗读，间隔15秒。最后一次阅读将再次以正常速度完成，在此期间您应该检查您的工作。然后您将有一分钟的时间再次检查您的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: Decide which of the words given in the box below would best complete the passage if inserted in the corresponding blank. The words can be used ONCE ONLY. Mark the letter for each word on ANSWER SHEET TWO.

Edward Hopper (1882-1967) is something of a success, if only his success had come swifter. At the age of 40, he was a failing artist who (31) ______ to sell a single painting. As he approached 80, Time magazine (32) ______ him on its cover. Today, half a century after his death, Hopper is considered a giant of modern expression, with an uncanny, unforgettable, and utterly (33) ______ sense for mood and place.

Much of Hopper’s work excavates modern city experience. In canvas (34) ______ canvas, he depicts diners, cafes, streetlights, gas stations, train stations, and hotel rooms. The scenes are marked by vivid color juxtapositions and stark, theatrical lighting, as well as by harshly contoured figures, who appear at once part of, and (35) ______ to, their surroundings. The ambiance throughout his repertoire is of loneliness, and psychological tension, whereas his rural or coastal scenes offer a strong (36) ______ of tranquility or optimism.

Realistic (37) ______ they may seem, Edward Hopper’s paintings are not mere representations of supposed reality. They deconstruct and reconstruct the real, transforming it beyond the purely experiential. Like the views Hopper regularly included as pictures within his pictures, a characteristic Hopper composition is not first and foremost an image of (38) ______ fact but rather a gestalt created out of breakdown and fracture in the process of perception and indeed the capacity to perceive. His works have (39) ______ been dubbed metaphors of silence. Just as all utterance is governed by what remains unsaid, and by silence, so too Hopper’s art has its center of gravity in what is not actually visible in the paintings. Hopper’s art enacts ways of seeing and understanding that anchor (40) ______ situations in profound depths.

In this section there are three passages followed by ten multiple choice questions. For each multiple choice question, there are four suggested answers marked A, B, C and D. Choose the one that you think is the best answer and mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节由三篇文章组成，后面是十个多项选择题。对于每个多项选择题，有四个建议答案，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。选择您认为最佳答案的一个，并将您的答案标记在答题表二上。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Pairing the words “baby” and “sleep” can evoke strong emotions. Those who have had limited contact with little ones might interpret this word-combination as implying deep and prolonged slumber. For others, this union of words may elicit memories of prolonged periods of chaotic sleep (or what can feel like no sleep at all).
paragraphs.translationZh: （1）“宝贝”和“睡觉”这两个词配对可以唤起强烈的情绪。那些与小孩子接触有限的人可能会将这个词组合解释为暗示深度和长时间的睡眠。对于其他人来说，这种词语的结合可能会唤起长时间混乱睡眠的记忆（或者感觉根本没有睡觉）。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) Coping with the way babies sleep can be difficult. It’s not that babies don’t sleep. In fact, they sleep more than at any other stage of life. It’s more an issue of when they sleep. Newborns start by sleeping and waking around the clock. This is not always easy for parents. There is even research suggesting that in adults waking repeatedly at night can feel as bad as getting hardly any sleep in terms of attentional skills, fatigue levels and symptoms of depression.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 应对婴儿的睡眠方式可能很困难。这并不是说婴儿不睡觉。事实上，他们的睡眠时间比生命中任何其他阶段都多。这更多的是他们什么时候睡觉的问题。新生儿从昼夜不停地睡觉和醒来开始。这对父母来说并不总是那么容易。甚至有研究表明，成年人在夜间反复醒来，在注意力、疲劳程度和抑郁症状方面都会感觉与几乎没有睡眠一样糟糕。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) As to why infants wake at night, this is best explained by thinking about the two things that govern our sleep: the homeostatic and circadian processes. The crux of the homeostatic process is the straightforward idea that the longer we have been awake the greater our sleep drive (and the more sleepy we feel). It may take an adult an entire day to build up enough sleep drive to fall asleep at bedtime, but an infant may only need an hour or two of wakefulness before being able to drift off to sleep.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 至于为什么婴儿在晚上醒来，最好通过思考控制我们睡眠的两件事来解释：稳态过程和昼夜节律过程。体内平衡过程的关键是一个简单的想法，即我们清醒的时间越长，我们的睡眠动力就越大（并且我们感到越困）。成年人可能需要一整天的时间才能建立足够的睡眠动力才能在就寝时间入睡，但婴儿可能只需要一两个小时的清醒就可以入睡。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) The second process is circadian, which works like a clock. Adults typically feel more awake during the morning hours and sleepy at night, regardless of when we last slept. In very young babies this process is not yet developed. This means that sleep is more likely to occur at different points across the 24hour day.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4)第二个过程是昼夜节律，它的工作原理就像一个时钟。成年人通常在早上感觉更清醒，在晚上感觉更困，无论我们上次睡觉是什么时候。在非常小的婴儿中，这个过程尚未发育。这意味着睡眠更有可能发生在一天 24 小时的不同时间点。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) Practically speaking, the immaturity of these two processes means that that newborn babies are actually expected to wake at night: they are doing exactly what they are supposed to do! They start life with small stomachs which need to be filled regularly so your child can gain strength and stay hydrated, so it’s a good thing that they are waking regularly to feed. As hard as disturbed sleep can be for caregivers, a waking baby is a good thing.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 实际上，这两个过程的不成熟意味着新生婴儿实际上应该在晚上醒来：他们正在做他们应该做的事情！他们一开始的胃很小，需要定期填满，这样你的孩子才能获得力量并保持水分，所以他们定期醒来进食是一件好事。尽管睡眠不安对护理人员来说可能很困难，但醒来的婴儿却是一件好事。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) But how long might this continue? The parenting mantra “this too shall pass” is true when it comes to dealing with certain aspects of a baby’s sleep. Night wakings typically become less frequent as an infant grows up, and sleep changes in other ways throughout a person’s life. For example, sleep length reduces and there are changes in sleep architecture (or composition of Rapid Eye Movement, REM, and Non-Rapid Eye Movement, NREM, sleep). A premature baby’s sleep cycle might take just 45 minutes, whereas an adult’s can be double that at 90 minutes. Other changes also occur; for example, whereas babies’ sleep cycles start with REM-like sleep, adults start with NREM sleep.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 但是这种情况会持续多久呢？在处理婴儿睡眠的某些方面时，“这也会过去”这句育儿格言是正确的。随着婴儿的成长，夜间醒来的频率通常会降低，而睡眠在人的一生中也会以其他方式发生变化。例如，睡眠时间缩短，睡眠结构（或快速眼动睡眠和非快速眼动睡眠的组成）发生变化。早产儿的睡眠周期可能只需要 45 分钟，而成人的睡眠周期可能是 90 分钟的两倍。其他变化也会发生；例如，婴儿的睡眠周期从类快速眼动睡眠开始，而成人则从非快速眼动睡眠开始。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) For some parents, knowing that sleep changes throughout life is enough to help them cope with an infant’s night awakenings. In fact, sleep education alone can help some parents to deal with infant sleep. Other parents want more detailed information, such as about babies’ sleep schedules, bedtime routines, sleep problems, sleep safety, sleep environment, naps, sleep training, and special circumstances. We provide all this information, and more, on our website, where physicians, psychologists, and researchers from the Pediatric Sleep Council have also answered hundreds of questions about sleep via video and text.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 对于一些父母来说，了解一生中睡眠的变化足以帮助他们应对婴儿夜间醒来的问题。事实上，仅睡眠教育就可以帮助一些家长应对婴儿睡眠问题。其他家长想要更详细的信息，例如婴儿的睡眠时间表、就寝时间、睡眠问题、睡眠安全、睡眠环境、小睡、睡眠训练和特殊情况。我们在我们的网站上提供所有这些信息以及更多信息，儿科睡眠委员会的医生、心理学家和研究人员还通过视频和文本回答了数百个有关睡眠的问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) Remember: sleep matters. Experts agree that sleep is essential for health, growth and general development. It is important not just for babies, but for parents too. If we can improve sleep within a family, and create a happy association between the words “baby” and “sleep”, then the Pediatric Sleep Council has achieved its goal.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8)记住：睡眠很重要。专家们一致认为，睡眠对于健康、成长和全面发展至关重要。这不仅对婴儿很重要，对父母也很重要。如果我们能够改善家庭内部的睡眠，并在“宝宝”和“睡眠”这两个词之间建立起愉快的联系，那么儿科睡眠委员会就达到了它的目标。

paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 关于婴儿睡眠，以下哪项陈述是正确的？

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Which of the following is the most appropriate title for the passage?
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 下列哪项是该文章的最合适的标题？

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Roie Galitz’s adventurous spirit has quite literally driven him to the ends of the Earth. He has made several excursions to the Arctic islands of Svalbard and the ice sheets of Antarctica. He has also been to the snowy plain of Norway and the wild waters of Kamchatka, Russia — all in the hopes of capturing some of the Earth’s most elusive creatures.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 罗伊·加利茨的冒险精神确实驱使他到达了地球的尽头。他曾多次游览北极的斯瓦尔巴群岛和南极洲的冰盖。他还去过挪威的雪原和俄罗斯堪察加半岛的狂野水域——所有这些都是为了捕捉地球上一些最难以捉摸的生物。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) The photographer comes from Tel Aviv, Israel. He first fell in love with wildlife photography in the sweltering savannas of Tanzania, Africa. Galitz says he prefers to work in the cold — even when that can mean temperatures as low as 40 degrees below zero. He layers up multiple pairs of long trousers, fleece shirts and the thickest wool socks he can find. On top of all of that, he wears an 8-pound Arctic suit. “When you’re cold, you can always put on an extra layer,” he says. “But when you’re hot, there is a legal limit to how much you can remove.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 摄影师来自以色列特拉维夫。他第一次爱上野生动物摄影是在非洲坦桑尼亚闷热的大草原上。加利茨说，他更喜欢在寒冷的环境下工作——即使这意味着气温可能低至零下 40 度。他把多条长裤、羊毛衬衫和他能找到的最厚的羊毛袜子叠起来。最重要的是，他还穿着一套 8 磅重的北极套装。 “当你冷的时候，你总是可以多穿一层，”他说。 “但是当你很热的时候，你可以去除的数量是有法律限制的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) Extreme environments are also where he finds his favorite photography subjects: animals that are rarely viewed in the wild.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 极端的环境也是他最喜欢的摄影题材：在野外很少见到的动物。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) “If I showed things that have been viewed time and time again, it wouldn’t be special. It wouldn’t be unique,” Galitz says. “It would just be like photographing a sparrow. Who cares about a sparrow? Everybody sees them all the time. As a photographer, I always try to find what has been done, what hasn’t been done, why it hasn’t been done — then try to do it.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) “如果我展示的东西已经被反复浏览过，那它就不会很特别。它不会是独一无二的，”加利茨说。 “这就像拍摄一只麻雀。谁在乎麻雀？每个人都经常看到它们。作为一名摄影师，我总是试图找出已经做过的事情，还没有做过的事情，为什么没有做过——然后尝试去做。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) One photo that captures Galitz’s quest features a polar bear with a live seal in its grasp. This moment of the hunt had rarely, if ever, been photographed before. Local bear experts doubted that Galitz would be able to get the shot. But after a long night of silently kneeling on the ice, fighting to stay warm but remaining still so as not to disturb the seals swimming below — he got the shot.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 一张记录了加利茨探索的照片中，一只北极熊手里抓着一只活海豹。以前很少有人拍到这一狩猎时刻。当地的熊专家怀疑加利茨是否能够拍摄到照片。但在漫长的一夜里，他默默地跪在冰面上，努力保暖，但又保持不动，以免打扰下面游泳的海豹——他终于成功了。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) Venturing into the wild comes with some risk, from frostbite to close encounters with bears and walruses. Galitz takes it all in stride. A minor case of frostbite in the Arctic is like getting a sunburn at the beach, he says. And the cold forces him to be resourceful. On multiple occasions, he has used his nose to operate the touch screen on his camera. Sometimes, though, he will quickly remove his gloves to snap the shot.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 冒险进入野外会带来一些风险，从冻伤到与熊和海象的亲密接触。加利茨对这一切泰然处之。他说，北极地区的轻微冻伤就像在海滩上晒伤一样。寒冷迫使他必须足智多谋。他曾多次用鼻子来操作相机上的触摸屏。不过，有时他会迅速摘下手套进行拍摄。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) Wildlife photography requires a certain spirit, Galitz says. For many of the far-off places he chooses to shoot, he has to obtain production permits and coordinate the often-complicated logistics of getting there. But the planning pays off, he says, when he gets the perfect shot. In a photo titled “Polar Bear Family Hug”, he captured two cubs and a mother bear in a moment of vulnerability as they awoke from a nap.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 加利茨说，野生动物摄影需要一定的精神。对于他选择的许多偏远地点进行拍摄，他必须获得制作许可并协调到达那里的后勤工作，这些后勤工作通常很复杂。但他说，当他得到完美的镜头时，计划就会得到回报。在一张题为“北极熊家庭拥抱”的照片中，他捕捉到了两只小熊和一只母熊从午睡中醒来时的脆弱时刻。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) “That’s actually the best compliment a wildlife photographer can ask for,” Galitz says. “Because when an animal is sleeping in front of you, it means she trusts you.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) “这实际上是野生动物摄影师所能要求的最好的赞美，”加利茨说。 “因为当动物睡在你面前时，就意味着她信任你。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) In another photo of brown bears playing together in Lake Kuril in Russia, Galitz laid low to the ground and took shot after shot. He was trying to capture the symmetry of the bears’ open mouths. “With wildlife, you control the scene by controlling yourself,” he says, referring to his position in relation to his furry subjects. You can’t tell a bear to strike a pose or turn toward the light. So for a wildlife photographer, Galitz explains, it’s all about the technique.
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 在俄罗斯千岛湖棕熊一起玩耍的另一张照片中，加利茨趴在地上，拍了一张又一张。他试图捕捉熊张开的嘴巴的对称性。 “对于野生动物，你可以通过控制自己来控制场景，”他说，指的是他与毛茸茸的拍摄对象之间的关系。你无法告诉熊摆出姿势或转向光线。加利茨解释说，对于野生动物摄影师来说，技术至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) In addition to stunning action shots, Galitz also looks to capture moments that will elicit specific feelings from the viewer. “When I’m photographing the animals, I’m trying to show their character, their soul,” he says. Many of his photos depict animals in moments of closeness — courting, parenting, cuddling — to demonstrate their individual personalities and familial relationships. “I’m trying to make people relate to animals in an intimate way, as I am relating to animals in an intimate way,” he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: (10) 除了令人惊叹的动作镜头外，加利茨还希望捕捉能引起观众特定感受的瞬间。 “当我拍摄动物时，我试图展现它们的性格和灵魂，”他说。他的许多照片描绘了动物的亲密时刻——求爱、养育、拥抱——以展示它们的个性和家庭关系。 “我试图让人们以亲密的方式与动物建立联系，就像我以亲密的方式与动物建立联系一样，”他说。

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) Galitz also regularly uses his photography to promote conservation efforts. Looking at his photos from year to year, he says he can see the world changing and the habitats of the animals he photographs disappearing. “My images are testimony,” he says. “This is what I saw last year, this is what I saw here, you can see the difference. We can’t ignore that.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (11) 加利茨还经常使用他的摄影来促进保护工作。他说，年复一年地看着他的照片，他可以看到世界在变化，他拍摄的动物的栖息地正在消失。 “我的图像就是证据，”他说。 “这是我去年看到的，这也是我在这里看到的，你可以看到差异。我们不能忽视这一点。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) It was a big, squarish frame house that had once been white, decorated with cupolas and spires and scrolled balconies in the heavily lightsome style of the seventies, set on what had once been our most select street. But garages and cotton gins had encroached and obliterated even the names of that neighborhood; only Miss Emily’s house was left, lifting its stubborn and coquettish decay above the cotton wagons and the gasoline pumps — an eyesore among eyesores.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 这是一座巨大的方形框架房子，曾经是白色的，装饰有圆顶、尖顶和卷轴阳台，具有七十年代的轻盈风格，坐落在我们曾经最选择的街道上。但车库和轧棉机甚至侵占并抹去了那个街区的名字；只剩下艾米丽小姐的房子，它那顽固而妖艳的腐朽痕迹，在棉花车和汽油泵之上——令人眼花缭乱。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) Alive, Miss Emily had been a tradition, a duty, and a care; a sort of hereditary obligation upon the town, dating from that day in 1894 when Colonel Sartoris, the mayor — he who fathered the edict that no Negro woman should appear on the streets without an apron-remitted her taxes, the dispensation dating from the death of her father on into perpetuity. Not that Miss Emily would have accepted charity. Colonel Sartoris invented an involved tale to the effect that Miss Emily’s father had loaned money to the town, which the town, as a matter of business, preferred this way of repaying. Only a man of Colonel Sartoris’ generation and thought could have invented it, and only a woman could have believed it.
paragraphs.translationZh: （2）艾米丽小姐活着，就是一种传统，一种责任，一种关怀；镇上的一种世袭义务，可以追溯到1894年的那一天，当时市长萨托里斯上校——他制定了禁止黑人妇女不戴围裙出现在街上的法令——免除了她的税款，这项豁免从她父亲去世后就永久有效。并不是说艾米丽小姐会接受施舍。萨托里斯上校编造了一个复杂的故事，大意是艾米丽小姐的父亲向镇上借了钱，而镇上出于生意上的考虑，更喜欢这种偿还方式。只有萨托里斯上校那个时代和思想的人才能发明它，也只有女人才能相信它。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) When the next generation, with its more modern ideas, became mayors and aldermen, this arrangement created some little dissatisfaction. On the first of the year they mailed her a tax notice. February came, and there was no reply. They wrote her a formal letter, asking her to call at the sheriff’s office at her convenience. A week later the mayor wrote her himself, offering to call or to send his car for her, and received in reply a note on paper of an archaic shape, in a thin, flowing calligraphy in faded ink, to the effect that she no longer went out at all. The tax notice was also enclosed, without comment.
paragraphs.translationZh: （3）当思想更加现代的下一代成为市长和市议员时，这种安排引起了一些小小的不满。今年第一天，他们给她寄了一张纳税通知单。二月到了，却没有任何回音。他们给她写了一封正式的信，要求她在方便的时候致电治安官办公室。一周后，市长亲自写信给她，主动提出打电话或派车来接她，并收到了一张回信，纸条写在一张老式的纸上，用褪色的墨水写着薄薄的、流畅的书法，大意是她不再出门了。税务通知也随函附上，但没有发表评论。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) They called a special meeting of the Board of Aldermen. A delegation waited upon her, knocked at the door through which no visitor had passed since she ceased giving china-painting lessons eight or ten years earlier. They were admitted by the old Negro into a dim hall from which a stairway mounted into still more shadow. It smelled of dust and disuse — a close, dank smell. The Negro led them into the parlor. It was furnished in heavy, leather-covered furniture. When the Negro opened the blinds of one window, they could see that the leather was cracked; and when they sat down, a faint dust rose sluggishly about their thighs, spinning with slow motes in the single sunray. On a tarnished gilt easel before the fireplace stood a crayon portrait of Miss Emily’s father.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 他们召开了市议员委员会特别会议。一个代表团正在等候她，敲着那扇门，自从她八、十年前停止教授瓷器画课程以来，就没有再有人进过这扇门。老黑人把他们领进了一个昏暗的大厅，从那里有一段楼梯进入了更多的阴影。它闻起来有灰尘和废弃的味道——一种接近、潮湿的气味。黑人领着他们走进客厅。房间里摆满了厚重的皮革家具。当黑人打开一扇窗户的百叶窗时，他们可以看到皮革已经裂开了；当他们坐下时，一股微弱的灰尘在他们的大腿周围缓慢地升起，在单一的阳光下缓慢地旋转着。壁炉前一个失去光泽的镀金画架上放着艾米丽小姐父亲的蜡笔肖像。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) They rose when she entered-a small, fat woman in black, with a thin gold chain descending to her waist and vanishing into her belt, leaning on an ebony cane with a tarnished gold head. Her skeleton was small and spare; perhaps that was why what would have been merely plumpness in another was obesity in her. She looked bloated, like a body long submerged in motionless water, and of that pallid hue. Her eyes, lost in the fatty ridges of her face, looked like two small pieces of coal pressed into a lump of dough as they moved from one face to another while the visitors stated their errand.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 当她进来时，他们站了起来——一个身材矮小、肥胖的黑衣女人，一条细金链垂到腰间，消失在腰带里，拄着一根乌木手杖，手杖的金头已经失去光泽。她的骨架又小又瘦；也许这就是为什么在别人看来只是丰满的她在她身上却是肥胖的。她看起来臃肿不堪，就像一具长期浸泡在静止水中的尸体，而且颜色苍白。当来访者陈述他们的任务时，她的眼睛迷失在脸上的脂肪脊中，看起来就像两小块煤炭被压成一团面团，从一张脸移动到另一张脸。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) She did not ask them to sit. She just stood in the door and listened quietly until the spokesman came to a stumbling halt. Then they could hear the invisible watch ticking at the end of the gold chain.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 她没有请他们坐下。她只是站在门口静静地听着，直到发言人踉踉跄跄地停了下来。然后他们就能听到金链末端隐形手表的滴答声。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) Her voice was dry and cold. “I have no taxes in Jefferson. Colonel Sartoris explained it to me. Perhaps one of you can gain access to the city records and satisfy yourselves.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 她的声音干燥而冰冷。 “我在杰斐逊没有缴税。萨托里斯上校向我解释了这一点。也许你们中的一个人可以查阅该市的记录并满足自己。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) “But we have. We are the city authorities, Miss Emily. Didn’t you get a notice from the sheriff, signed by him?”
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) “但是我们有。我们是市政府当局，艾米丽小姐。你没有收到警长的通知吗，有他签字吗？”

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) “I received a paper, yes,” Miss Emily said. “Perhaps he considers himself the sherif... I have no taxes in Jefferson.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) “是的，我收到了一篇论文，”艾米丽小姐说。 “也许他认为自己是治安官……我在杰斐逊没有纳税。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) “But there is nothing on the books to show that, you see. We must go by the…”
paragraphs.translationZh: (10) “但你看，书本上没有任何内容表明这一点。我们必须遵循……”

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) “See Colonel Sartoris. I have no taxes in Jefferson.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (11) “请见萨托里斯上校。我在杰斐逊没有缴税。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (12) “But, Miss Emily…”
paragraphs.translationZh: (12)“但是，艾米丽小姐……”

paragraphs.sourceText: (13) “See Colonel Sartoris.(Colonel Sartoris had been dead almost ten years.) I have no taxes in Jefferson. Tobe!” The Negro appeared. “Show these gentlemen out.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (13)“见萨托里斯上校。（萨托里斯上校已经去世近十年了。）我在杰斐逊没有纳税。托比！”黑人出现了。 “带这些先生出去。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Read carefully the following excerpt on teacher quality assessment, and then write your response in NO LESS THAN 200 WORDS, in which you should:

paragraphs.sourceText: You can support yourself with information from the excerpt.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您可以使用摘录中的信息来支持自己。

paragraphs.sourceText: Marks will be awarded for content relevance, content sufficiency, organization and language quality. Failure to follow the above instructions may result in a loss of marks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 将根据内容相关性、内容充分性、组织和语言质量给予分数。不遵守上述说明可能会导致分数丢失。

paragraphs.sourceText: Write your response on ANSWER SHEET THREE.
paragraphs.translationZh: 将您的回答写在答题表三上。

paragraphs.sourceText: Teacher quality assessment commonly includes reviews of qualifications, tests of teaching quality, and observations of teaching practice. Assessments of teacher quality are currently used for policy making, employment, merit-based pay awards, and as data to inform the professional growth of teachers, etc.
paragraphs.translationZh: 教师素质评估通常包括资格审查、教学质量测试和教学实践观察。教师素质评估目前用于政策制定、就业、绩效工资奖励以及作为教师专业成长的数据等。

paragraphs.sourceText: Teacher qualifications include a range of variables affecting teacher quality: type of teaching certification, undergraduate major or minor, undergraduate institution, advanced degree(s) or certifications, type of preparation program, test scores, and years of teaching experience. In many countries, teaching credentials represent the main measure of teacher quality and serve as a threshold of holding teaching positions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 教师资格包括一系列影响教师质量的变量：教学认证类型、本科专业或辅修专业、本科院校、高级学位或认证、预备课程类型、考试成绩和教学经验年限。在许多国家，教学资格是衡量教师素质的主要标准，也是担任教学职位的门槛。

paragraphs.sourceText: Teacher quality with regard to student achievement — also known as “teacher effectiveness”-is measured in terms of student achievement gains. Student achievement is measured through the use of standardized tests to determine the academic growth of students over time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与学生成绩相关的教师质量——也称为“教师效能”——是根据学生成绩的提高来衡量的。学生的成绩是通过使用标准化测试来衡量的，以确定学生随时间的学业进步。

paragraphs.sourceText: Assessments of teacher quality may also draw upon evidence collected from observations of teachers’ work that lead to the growth of effective teachers. This evidence may be collected from in-person or video recorded observations of teaching, pre- and post-observation conferences with teachers, and samples of teachers’ work with students. Assessments of teacher practice may examine teacher quality for a single lesson or over an entire school year. Such assessments may be impression-based or narrative in form but have become increasingly more common in teacher quality assessment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对教师质量的评估也可以利用从对教师工作的观察中收集的证据，这些证据可以促进高效教师的成长。这些证据可以从现场或视频记录的教学观察、观察前和观察后与教师的会议以及教师与学生的工作样本中收集。对教师实践的评估可以检查单节课或整个学年的教师质量。这种评估可能是基于印象的或叙述性的，但在教师质量评估中变得越来越普遍。

paragraphs.sourceText: Decide which of the words given in the box below would best complete the passage if inserted in the corresponding blank. The words can be used ONCE ONLY. Mark the letter for each word on ANSWER SHEET TWO.

As a library curator of literary and historical manuscripts and letters, I spend my days in the company of the respectable dead. I’m not the one who brought them together or decided which individuals deserved a place in the magic circle. I serve (31) ______ in the roles of custodian and interpreter, mindful that I am the latest in a long line of collectors and librarians who have cared for the manuscripts of figures from the past. I’ve learned from them, argued with them, and — yes — loved them, not because they were. (32) ______ but because they were humans, and because they granted me such rich works of art.
